proteins.name: IL1RN
proteins.summary: The IL-1 receptor antagonist binds IL-1R1 and blocks IL-1 signalling. IL-1Ra knockout mice have much larger infarcts after transient cerebral ischaemia, with microglia as the protective source, and develop EAE without pertussis toxin. In mouse mixed glial cultures recombinant IL-1Ra abolishes IL-1beta-induced IL-6, NF-kB and MAPK activation.
links: Inhibits the IL-1 receptor (IL1R) in astrocytes and microglia (top-level map).
Binds IL1R1 into its own complex, IL1RN:IL1R1, beside IL-1beta binding (Astrocyte signaling).

Matsuki T et al. 2006, Int Immunol.
Berglöf E et al. 2003, J Neuroimmunol.
Schreuder H et al. 1995, FEBS Lett.

diseases.model: IL-1Ra (Il1rn) knockout mice, intracerebroventricular infusion of human oligomeric Abeta1-42
diseases.shows: Loss of endogenous IL-1Ra worsens Abeta-induced microglial activation and neuronal damage in the hippocampus, i.e. IL-1Ra restrains IL-1-driven glial activation in an AD-like model.
diseases.cite: Craft JM et al. 2005, J Neuroinflammation.

diseases.model: IL-1Ra (Il1rn) knockout and caspase-1 knockout mice, aging, substantia nigra
diseases.shows: IL-1Ra knockout mice, with no other insult, show age-related loss of nigral dopamine neurons, more activated microglia and worse motor skills, so endogenous IL-1Ra protects dopaminergic neurons by limiting IL-1 signalling.
diseases.cite: Stojakovic A et al. 2016, Mol Neurobiol.

diseases.model: IL-1Ra-deficient and IL-1-deficient mice, MOG-induced EAE
diseases.shows: Imbalance of the IL-1/IL-1Ra system drives EAE: IL-1Ra deficiency gives severe disease while IL-1 deficiency protects, showing IL-1Ra blockade of IL-1R1 signalling limits autoimmune neuroinflammation.
diseases.cite: Matsuki T et al. 2006, Int Immunol.

proteins.name: OSM
proteins.summary: Oncostatin M, made by CNS myeloid cells, acts on astrocytes and brain endothelium through its receptor OSMR with gp130. It induces IL-6 and STAT1/STAT3 activation in astrocytes and lowers claudin-5 and VE-cadherin in inflamed brain endothelial cells, and the OSM-OSMR axis shapes EAE, BBB leakage and cuprizone demyelination in mice.
links: Binds JAK:OSMR:IL6ST on astrocytes and on endothelial cells: OSMR with gp130 (IL6ST) and the kinases JAK1 and JAK2, which sit on the receptor chains before OSM binds (Hermanns 1999) (top-level map, Astrocyte signaling, altered BBB permeability).

In astrocytes the bound receptor activates JAK-STAT signalling (STAT1 and STAT3 phosphorylation, Hsu 2015) and MAPK signalling (ERK1/2 and p38, which carry its induction of IL6, Van Wagoner 2000); IL6 transcription is reached through the MAPK signalling already drawn, not by a direct arc.
In endothelial cells it lowers claudin-5 (and VE-cadherin, not on the map) by a mechanism not shown: unknown process (?) (altered BBB permeability).

OSM receptor signalling raises CCL20 in brain endothelial cells and astrocytes (primary human and mouse cells), and CCL20 promotes Th17 cell adhesion through LFA-1 (top-level map, Hermans 2022, read in full). OSM does not raise VCAM-1 or ICAM-1 and lowers them under inflammation.

diseases.shows: Myeloid-derived OSM acts on OSMR at the blood-brain barrier, lowering claudin-5 and ZO-1 and letting leukocytes in; OSM is raised in MS lesions and OSMR deficiency protects, matching the drawn OSM-OSMR edge.
diseases.cite: Hermans D et al. 2022, Acta Neuropathol.

proteins.name: OSMR
proteins.summary: The oncostatin M receptor. Primary mouse astrocytes express OSMR and phosphorylate STAT1 and STAT3 on OSM, while microglia do not. Astrocyte-specific OsmR deletion worsens EAE, and OSMRbeta-deficient mice show less BBB leakage and Th17 infiltration.
links: Drawn as the complex JAK:OSMR:IL6ST: OSMR with gp130 (IL6ST), the type II OSM receptor, which OSM uses in astrocytes (Van Wagoner 2000), with JAK1 and JAK2 bound to the receptor chains (Stahl 1994, Hermanns 1999), as the map draws JAK:IFNGR. Astrocytes carry it, microglia do not (Hsu 2015).
Top-level map: to JAK-STAT SIGNALING and MAPK SIGNALING in astrocytes, to BBB PERMEABILITY in endothelial cells.

diseases.shows: OSMR acts specifically in astrocytes to reduce EAE severity, establishing the myeloid-OSM to astrocyte-OSMR axis in vivo; note the net effect here is protective, whereas the map draws OSM/OSMR as inflammatory.

proteins.name: SOCS1
proteins.summary: Suppressor of cytokine signalling 1 limits interferon signalling in glia. SOCS1 expressed in oligodendrocytes (PLP/SOCS1 mice) lowers their IFN-gamma responsiveness and changes the course of EAE. In primary mouse astrocytes interferon induces SOCS1, and SOCS1 knockdown raises interferon-induced CXCL10, CCL2 and CCL5.
links: Inhibits JAK-STAT signalling in oligodendrocytes (top-level map): SOCS1 acts on the JAK/STAT1 step below the IFN-gamma receptor, not on the receptor (Balabanov 2006, read in full).

Its transcription is stimulated by JAK-STAT signalling, and it inhibits JAK-STAT signalling in astrocytes, drawn as the map draws SOCS3 (Astrocyte signaling); it acts at the receptor and JAKs, not on the CXCL10 gene.

refs.cite: Balabanov R et al. 2006, J Neurosci.
Balabanov R et al. 2007, J Neurosci.
Qin H et al. 2008, J Immunol.
Kim JH et al. 2014, Exp Neurobiol.

diseases.model: N9 microglial cells exposed to Abeta, SOCS1 siRNA
diseases.shows: SOCS1 knockdown abolishes the shift of Abeta-activated microglia away from the pro-inflammatory state, showing SOCS1 limits Abeta-driven microglial inflammation; weak evidence (microglial cell line, no in vivo AD model).
diseases.cite: Cai H et al. 2016, Neural Plast.

diseases.model: PLP/SOCS1 transgenic mice (SOCS1 in oligodendrocytes), MOG-induced EAE
diseases.shows: Oligodendrocyte SOCS1 lowers IFN-gamma responsiveness of oligodendrocytes and changes the course of EAE, showing SOCS1 limits interferon signalling in glia in an MS model.
diseases.cite: Balabanov R et al. 2007, J Neurosci.

proteins.name: TAB2
proteins.summary: TAB2 links upstream signals to TAK1. In primary mouse microglia K63 ubiquitination of TAB2 drives TAB1-TAK1-TAB2 complex formation and NF-kB activation, and microglia-specific Tab2 knockdown protects dopaminergic neurons in MPTP mice. TAB2 knockdown also reduces injury after ischaemic stroke.
links: Driven by JAK-STAT signalling (STAT3 binds the TAB2 promoter, ChIP; a STAT3 inhibitor lowers TAB2 in primary microglia and in vivo) and drives NF-kB signalling in microglia (top-level map, Zhao 2026, read in full). TAB2 binds K63-linked ubiquitin through its zinc finger and assembles TAK1; it does not drive MAPK here.

refs.cite: Zhao Y et al. 2026, Adv Sci (Weinh).
Xia Q et al. 2022, Exp Mol Med.
Li Z et al. 2023, Adv Sci (Weinh).

diseases.model: Primary mouse microglia and a mouse PD model; microglia-specific Tab2 knockdown
diseases.shows: K63 ubiquitination of TAB2 drives TAB1-TAK1-TAB2 complex formation and NF-kB activation in microglia, and microglial Tab2 knockdown protects dopaminergic neurons, matching the drawn TAB2-TAK1 edge.
diseases.cite: Zhao Y et al. 2026, Adv Sci (Weinh).

proteins.name: ACKR1
proteins.summary: The atypical chemokine receptor ACKR1 (Darc) shuttles chemokines across endothelium. In mouse EAE its expression in blood-brain barrier endothelial cells depends on endothelial IL-1R1 signalling.
links: IL-1 receptor signalling in brain endothelial cells lowers heme oxygenase-1 (HMOX1), which keeps ACKR1 (DARC) down, so IL-1 raises ACKR1 (top-level map; endothelial Il1r1 and Hmox1 deletion and HO-1 overexpression, Hauptmann 2020).

refs.cite: Hauptmann J et al. 2020, Acta Neuropathol.

diseases.model: EAE; endothelial Il1r1-deficient mice, blood-brain barrier endothelium
diseases.shows: Endothelial IL-1R1 signalling drives ACKR1 (Darc) expression in blood-brain barrier endothelial cells during EAE, the chemokine-shuttling step the map draws.
diseases.cite: Hauptmann J et al. 2020, Acta Neuropathol.

proteins.name: GRN
proteins.summary: Progranulin restrains microglial activation. Microglia-specific progranulin deletion in mice raises NF-kB activity and TNF, and progranulin-deficient microglia make more C1q and C3 and prune inhibitory synapses. Progranulin-deficient mice also show more microgliosis and neuron loss after MPTP.
links: Lowers NF-kB signalling in microglia (top-level map): microglial progranulin loss raises TNF-induced NF-kB activity, which needs microglial IKBKB (Krabbe 2017, read in full); TNF itself was not measured.
Progranulin loss raises C1q production; the mechanism is not established, so the step is an unknown process (?) (Microglial phagocytosis).

refs.cite: Krabbe G et al. 2017, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A.
Lui H et al. 2016, Cell.
Martens LH et al. 2012, J Clin Invest.

diseases.model: 5xFAD mice, intrahippocampal progranulin protein; microglia isolated from 5xFAD brains
diseases.shows: Progranulin administration lowers Abeta plaques, downregulates BACE1 and improves microglial Abeta phagocytosis in 5xFAD mice, consistent with progranulin restraining microglial/amyloid pathology.
diseases.cite: Guan Z et al. 2020, Front Cell Neurosci.

diseases.model: MPTP mouse model of PD, progranulin gene delivery (overexpression)
diseases.shows: Progranulin gene delivery protects nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons in the MPTP model, showing progranulin acts as an anti-inflammatory/neurotrophic brake in a PD model.
diseases.cite: Van Kampen JM et al. 2014, PLoS One.

diseases.model: Grn-deficient mice, cuprizone/toxin-induced demyelination; microglia
diseases.shows: Progranulin deficiency causes sex-dependent changes in the microglial response to demyelination and myelination defects, showing progranulin regulates microglia during demyelinating injury.
diseases.cite: Zhang T et al. 2023, Acta Neuropathol.

proteins.name: CTSD
proteins.summary: Cathepsin D is the main lysosomal aspartic protease of the brain. Its loss in mice turns microglia and astrocytes reactive, with iNOS and NO-driven neuronal death. Cathepsin D degrades alpha-synuclein in the neuronal lysosome (dopaminergic neurons) and tau (purified enzyme, neuroblastoma cells, CatD-knockout tauopathy mice), and its deficiency leads to insoluble alpha-synuclein and hyperphosphorylated tau.
links: Catalyses the degradation of alpha-synuclein in the neuronal lysosome, shown in dopaminergic neurons and Ctsd-knockout mice (Neuron signaling); it was drawn in the microglial phagolysosome before the full texts were read.
Catalyses the degradation of tau in neurons (MAPT cleavage).

Suzuki C et al. 2022, Sci Rep.

diseases.model: Cathepsin D (Ctsd) knockout mice; brain
diseases.shows: Genetic deletion of cathepsin D triggers prominent tauopathy and intracellular Abeta accumulation, showing the lysosomal protease is needed to clear AD-related proteins.
diseases.cite: Terron HM et al. 2024, Alzheimers Res Ther.

diseases.model: alpha-synucleinopathy cell and mouse models, recombinant pro-cathepsin D
diseases.shows: Recombinant pro-CTSD enhances degradation of alpha-synuclein in synucleinopathy models, the cathepsin D to alpha-synuclein step the map draws.
diseases.cite: Prieto Huarcaya S et al. 2022, Autophagy.

proteins.name: LDLR
proteins.summary: The LDL receptor takes up apoE and amyloid-beta in the brain. Brain LDLR overexpression lowers apoE by 50 to 90 percent, speeds amyloid-beta clearance and reduces microgliosis and astrogliosis in APP/PS1 mice, and it suppresses microglial activation in tauopathy mice. In primary astrocytes LDLR drives amyloid-beta uptake and lysosomal degradation.
links: Lowers extracellular apoE (top-level map). In Astrocyte signaling apoE binds LDLR, and the APOE:LDLR complex is taken up and degraded in lysosomes, one omitted process (//) (Kim 2009, Basak 2012).
Amyloid-beta 42 binds LDLR on the astrocyte membrane, independently of apoE (apoE-knockout astrocytes, Basak 2012); the complex goes to lysosomes, drawn as one omitted process (//) (APP processing).

refs.cite: Kim J et al. 2009, Neuron.
Shi Y et al. 2021, Neuron.
Basak JM et al. 2012, J Biol Chem.

diseases.model: LDLR overexpression in the brain of APP/PS1 amyloid mice; astrocytes
diseases.shows: Brain LDLR overexpression lowers apoE, speeds Abeta clearance and reduces amyloid deposition with less microgliosis and astrogliosis, the LDLR-apoE-Abeta uptake step the map draws.
diseases.cite: Kim J et al. 2009, Neuron.

proteins.name: LPL
proteins.summary: Lipoprotein lipase supports lipid uptake by microglia. Microglia-specific Lpl knockdown in mice lowers lipid uptake and phagocytic capacity, LPL activity rises in the mouse brain during remyelination, and LPL binds amyloid-beta and promotes its uptake by astrocytes and microglia.
links: Supports phagocytosis by microglia (top-level map).

LPL binds amyloid-beta 42 outside the cell (Nishitsuji 2011); the complex is taken up through sulfated glycosaminoglycans and degraded in lysosomes, one omitted process (//) (APP processing). LPL knockdown in microglia lowered uptake, not the degradation of what was taken up (Ma 2013).

Bruce KD et al. 2018, Front Mol Neurosci.
Loving BA et al. 2021, Cells.
Nishitsuji K et al. 2011, J Biol Chem.
Ma Y et al. 2013, Mol Cell Proteomics.

diseases.shows: LPL binds Abeta and promotes glycosaminoglycan-dependent cellular uptake of Abeta by astrocytes; weak as a disease paper (in vitro only, no AD animal model).

proteins.name: IGF1
proteins.summary: IGF-1 dampens astrocyte inflammation. In primary mouse astrocytes it lowers LPS-induced IL-6, IL-1beta and TNF, reduces TLR4 and blocks NF-kB p65 nuclear translocation, and it opposes TNF-driven NF-kB signalling in reactive astrocytes. The effect depends on time and sex in culture.
links: Lowers TLR4 and NF-kB signalling in astrocytes.

Pinto-Benito D et al. 2022, Glia.
Fernandez AM et al. 2012, Mol Psychiatry.
Grinberg YY et al. 2013, J Neurochem.

diseases.shows: IGF-1 regulation of calcineurin in astrocytes shapes amyloid pathology and glial inflammation, showing astrocytic IGF-1 signalling modifies AD pathology.
diseases.cite: Fernandez AM et al. 2011, Mol Psychiatry.

diseases.model: 6-OHDA rat parkinsonism, intrahippocampal RAd-IGF1 gene therapy
diseases.shows: IGF-1 gene therapy prevents memory deficits and modulates dopaminergic neurodegeneration and glial inflammation in a PD model, matching the drawn anti-inflammatory role of IGF-1.
diseases.cite: Herrera ML et al. 2024, Brain Behav Immun.

proteins.name: PKM
proteins.summary: Pyruvate kinase M2 sits in a glycolysis and histone lactylation loop that drives microglial dysfunction in 5XFAD mice, where microglia-specific Pkm2 ablation or PKM2 inhibition improves microglial function, amyloid burden and memory. PKM2-positive microglia are increased around plaques in human Alzheimer disease brain.
links: Drives glycolysis in microglia.

Lu N et al. 2025, J Neuroinflammation.

diseases.shows: A PKM2-glycolysis-H4K12 lactylation feedback loop drives microglial dysfunction in 5XFAD mice, and microglial Pkm2 ablation or PKM2 inhibition improves microglial function, the loop the map draws.
diseases.cite: Pan RY et al. 2022, Cell Metab.

diseases.model: Rotenone-treated BV2 microglia (PD cell model), PKM2 inhibitor shikonin
diseases.shows: PKM2-driven glycolytic flux produces methylglyoxal adducts that activate NF-kB in rotenone-exposed microglia, and PKM2 inhibition blocks it; weak (microglial cell line, no in vivo PD arm).
diseases.cite: Zhao Y et al. 2025, Cell Commun Signal.

proteins.name: LDHA
proteins.summary: Lactate dehydrogenase A turns glycolytic pyruvate into lactate. In microglia LDHA knockdown lowers glycolysis (extracellular acidification) and shifts them away from the pro-inflammatory state in an MPTP Parkinson model (Yan 2026). In female mice with EAE, microglial LDHA and its lactate are protective instead: microglia-specific Ldha deletion lowers H4K12 lactylation and worsens disease, and lactate raises GDNF and FGF1 (Li 2026, read in full). The two studies differ on whether LDHA loss is pro- or anti-inflammatory, so only its glycolytic role is drawn.
links: Drives glycolysis in microglia.

refs.cite: Li J et al. 2026, Nat Commun.
Yan W et al. 2026, Neuromolecular Med.

diseases.model: APP/PS1 mice, peri-plaque microglia; LDH inhibition with stiripentol
diseases.shows: LDHA is enriched in peri-plaque microglia and sustains the lactate rise with amyloid pathology; pharmacological LDH inhibition lowers interstitial Abeta and depletes peri-plaque microglia.
diseases.cite: Ashley CC et al. 2026, J Neuroinflammation.

diseases.model: MPTP-type mouse PD model and microglia; BMSC exosomal miR-1278 acting on Ldha
diseases.shows: Ldha-dependent microglial polarisation drives PD pathology, lowered by exosomal miR-1278; weak, since Ldha is targeted indirectly through a miRNA.
diseases.cite: Yan W et al. 2026, Neuromolecular Med.

diseases.model: EAE in female mice; microglial Ldha deletion
diseases.shows: A lactate-H4K12la-HDAC1 axis governs microglial state transitions in EAE, with microglial Ldha deletion changing microglial states and disease course.
diseases.cite: Li J et al. 2026, Nat Commun.

proteins.name: HIF1A
proteins.summary: IL-1beta induces HIF-1alpha and its target VEGF-A in human astrocytes and in mouse brain, and HIF-1alpha is needed for the VEGF-A response. Both proteins are found in reactive astrocytes of active multiple sclerosis lesions, and astrocytic VEGF-A drives BBB breakdown in EAE.
links: Induced by IL-1 receptor signalling (top-level map); in Astrocyte signaling its production under IL-1beta is an unknown process (?), as the paper shows the induction, not the path.

Drives VEGFA production in astrocytes (altered BBB permeability). In detail (small map HIF1A): HIF-1alpha binds ARNT, and HIF-1 drives VEGFA transcription from the HIF-1 site in its promoter (Forsythe 1996, Argaw 2006).
The outgoing top-level arc to VEGFA was removed (nuclear protein to secreted product).

refs.cite: Argaw AT et al. 2006, J Immunol.
Argaw AT et al. 2012, J Clin Invest.
Forsythe JA et al. 1996, Mol Cell Biol.

diseases.shows: Astrocytic HIF-1alpha-driven VEGF-A causes blood-brain barrier disruption in CNS inflammatory disease, and both proteins are found in reactive astrocytes of active MS lesions.
diseases.cite: Argaw AT et al. 2012, J Clin Invest.

proteins.name: BMAL1
proteins.summary: The clock protein BMAL1 restrains astrocyte activation. Astrocyte-specific Bmal1 deletion causes astrocyte activation and inflammatory gene expression in vivo, and Bmal1 deletion raises complement C3, mainly in astrocytes, through REV-ERBalpha, with more microglial synapse engulfment.
links: Drives NR1D1 (REV-ERBalpha) transcription; REV-ERBalpha lowers C3 transcription in astrocytes, drawn as a dashed (unknown) inhibition since the papers do not show whether it acts on the C3 gene directly (Astrocyte signaling, Griffin 2020). Kept off the top-level overview: a nuclear protein should not reach the extracellular C3 node.

Griffin P et al. 2020, Elife.

diseases.shows: The astrocyte circadian clock protein BMAL1 controls Chi3l1/YKL-40 and restrains glial activation and neuroinflammation in AD mice, matching the drawn role of BMAL1 restraining astrocyte activation.
diseases.cite: Lananna BV et al. 2020, Sci Transl Med.

diseases.shows: Neuronal Bmal1 deletion causes cell-autonomous loss of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive dopaminergic neurons, a PD-relevant phenotype; cell type differs from the astrocytic role the map draws.
diseases.cite: Kanan MF et al. 2024, JCI Insight.

diseases.model: EAE; myeloid-specific Bmal1 deletion (LysM-Cre)
diseases.shows: Loss of BMAL1 in myeloid cells exacerbates T cell-mediated CNS autoimmunity, with more immune cell accumulation and activation in EAE, i.e. BMAL1 restrains glial/myeloid activation in an MS model.
diseases.cite: Sutton CE et al. 2017, Nat Commun.

proteins.name: PTGS2
proteins.summary: Cyclooxygenase-2 makes the prostaglandin precursor for PGE2, and in the brain it is induced together with mPGES-1 in activated microglia. PGE2 acting through the microglial EP2 receptor raises COX-2 further. COX-2 deletion made LPS-induced neuroinflammation worse in mice, so COX-2 is drawn as the source of PGE2 only.
links: Produces PGE2 in microglia, induced through PTGER2 (EP2).

Fiebich BL et al. 1996, Glia.
Minghetti L et al. 1997, Eur J Neurosci.
Aid S et al. 2008, J Neuroinflammation.

diseases.shows: Selective COX-2 inhibition rescues Abeta-mediated suppression of synaptic plasticity and memory, showing COX-2 (and its prostaglandin product) mediates Abeta-driven dysfunction.
diseases.cite: Kotilinek LA et al. 2008, Brain.

diseases.model: MPTP mouse model of PD; COX-2-deficient mice, JNK2/JNK3 knockouts
diseases.shows: COX-2 is indispensable for MPTP-induced dopaminergic cell death, placing COX-2 downstream of JNK in PD neurodegeneration.
diseases.cite: Hunot S et al. 2004, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A.

diseases.model: TMEV-induced demyelinating disease (MS model), COX-2 inhibitors; COX-2-overexpressing and COX-2-knockout oligodendrocytes; human MS lesions
diseases.shows: COX-2 inhibitors limit demyelination in the TMEV MS model and COX-2 level sets oligodendrocyte vulnerability to excitotoxic death; cell type is oligodendrocytes, not the microglia the map draws.
diseases.cite: Carlson NG et al. 2010, J Neuroinflammation.

proteins.name: CXCL12
proteins.summary: CXCL12 (SDF-1) is made by CNS endothelium on the abluminal side of the blood-brain barrier. In primary mouse brain endothelial cells IFN-gamma lowers its transcript, while IL-1beta and IL-17 make the atypical receptor CXCR7 (ACKR3) take abluminal CXCL12 into the cell for lysosomal degradation, so CXCL12 on the brain side falls even though IL-1beta and TNF raise its transcript (Cruz-Orengo 2011, read in full). In mouse EAE abluminal CXCL12 holds CXCR4-positive leukocytes in perivascular cuffs; blocking CXCR7 keeps it there and lowers infiltration and disease. In rat spinal cord models CXCL12 activates astrocytes and microglia. Added as the missing partner of CXCR4, after it passed the bar by itself.
links: Lowered by IFN-gamma directly and by CXCR7 (ACKR3), which IL-1 and IL-17 receptor signalling drive, in endothelial cells; raised at the transcript level by TNF receptor signalling; binds CXCR4 on astrocytes and immune cells (top-level map).

McCandless EE et al. 2006, J Immunol.
Liu ZY et al. 2019, CNS Neurosci Ther.
Li XQ et al. 2016, PLoS One.
Shen W et al. 2014, J Neuroinflammation.

diseases.shows: Suppressing microglial CXCL12 blocks CXCR4+ B cell entry into the cortex and increases Abeta burden in 5xFAD mice, showing the CXCL12-CXCR4 axis is functional in AD.
diseases.cite: Zhang YL et al. 2025, Acta Pharmacol Sin.

diseases.model: A53T alpha-synuclein mice, primary microglia and BV-2 cells; PD patient brain tissue
diseases.shows: alpha-Synuclein raises microglial CXCL12 via TLR4/NF-kB and CXCL12/CXCR4/FAK/Src/Rac1 signalling drives microglial accumulation in the substantia nigra, the CXCL12-CXCR4 edge in a PD model.
diseases.cite: Li Y et al. 2019, J Neuroinflammation.

diseases.model: EAE; CXCL12 at the blood-brain barrier, CXCR4 blockade (AMD3100)
diseases.shows: Abluminal CXCL12 holds mononuclear infiltrates in the perivascular space during EAE; loss of this gradient lets leukocytes into the parenchyma.
diseases.cite: McCandless EE et al. 2006, J Immunol.

proteins.name: CXCR4
proteins.summary: CXCR4 is the CXCL12 receptor on astrocytes, microglia, neurons and infiltrating leukocytes. On astrocytes its activation releases TNF. In mouse EAE and West Nile virus encephalitis, blocking it lets leukocytes leave the perivascular space and enter the brain tissue, so CXCR4 signalling at the barrier restrains infiltration. Waited in the first check because its partner CXCL12 was not on the map; added together with CXCL12 once CXCL12 passed the same bar by itself.
links: Releases TNF from astrocytes; restrains leukocyte infiltration from immune cells (top-level map).

refs.cite: Bezzi P et al. 2001, Nat Neurosci.
McCandless EE et al. 2006, J Immunol.
McCandless EE et al. 2008, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A.
McCandless EE et al. 2008, Am J Pathol.

proteins.disease_note: The CXCL12-CXCR4 axis is protective in the AD and MS models (it brings in protective B cells, or holds infiltrates outside the parenchyma) and harmful in the PD model (it drives microglial accumulation).

diseases.model: 5xFAD and uMT/5xFAD mice; CXCR4 antagonist, microglial CXCL12 knockdown
diseases.shows: Blocking CXCR4 abolishes the protective infiltration of CXCR4+ memory B cells into the AD cortex, showing CXCR4 mediates the CXCL12 signal in an AD model.
diseases.cite: Zhang YL et al. 2025, Acta Pharmacol Sin.

diseases.model: A53T alpha-synuclein mice and primary microglia; CXCR4 pathway blockade
diseases.shows: CXCR4 is upregulated in substantia nigra microglia of A53T mice and CXCL12/CXCR4 signalling mediates alpha-synuclein-induced microglial accumulation.
diseases.cite: Li Y et al. 2019, J Neuroinflammation.

diseases.model: EAE; CXCR4 blockade with AMD3100
diseases.shows: CXCR4 engagement by abluminal CXCL12 keeps infiltrating leukocytes perivascular in EAE; blocking the receptor changes their entry into the parenchyma.
diseases.cite: McCandless EE et al. 2006, J Immunol.

proteins.name: CXCL13
proteins.summary: CXCL13 is made by neurons in the injured spinal cord and hippocampus. In mice it activates NF-kB and drives IL-6, IL-1beta and TNF through its receptor CXCR5, shown by neutralising antibody, knockdown, neuron-specific overexpression and Cxcr5 knockout mice. Waited in the first check because its partner its receptor CXCR5 was not on the map; added together with its receptor CXCR5 once its receptor CXCR5 passed the same bar by itself.
links: Binds CXCR5 on neurons (top-level map and Neuron signaling) and on astrocytes, where it activates MAPK signalling (ERK) (top-level map, Jiang 2016).

refs.cite: Wang J et al. 2023, J Neuroinflammation.
Shen Y et al. 2020, J Neuroinflammation.
Jiang BC et al. 2016, J Clin Invest.
Legler DF et al. 1998, J Exp Med.

diseases.model: Human MS CSF and actively demyelinating MS lesions
diseases.shows: CXCL13 is produced in active MS lesions and raised in MS CSF, where it is linked to recruitment of CXCR5-positive B and T cells, anchoring the drawn CXCL13-CXCR5 edge in MS; source is myeloid/stromal rather than neuronal as drawn.
diseases.cite: Krumbholz M et al. 2005, Brain.

proteins.name: CXCR5
proteins.summary: CXCR5 is induced in hippocampal microglia in mouse sepsis, where its knockout lowers p38 activation, IL-1beta, IL-6 and cognitive deficits, and in primary microglia its knockdown lowers LPS-induced p38 and NF-kB activation. In primary microglia NF-kB and STAT3 activation sit downstream of p38, and CXCR5 knockdown or knockout also raises autophagy. In spinal neurons it is needed for CXCL13 to activate NF-kB. In the retina and after stroke CXCR5 has been reported as protective, so its effect depends on the setting. Added as the missing partner of CXCL13, after it passed the bar by itself.
links: Binds CXCL13 on neurons and activates NF-kB signalling (top-level map and Neuron signaling).
On microglia CXCR5 drives MAPK signalling (p38), which drives NF-kB signalling (drawn as the existing MAPK to NF-kB arc; Shen 2021 read in full).

On astrocytes CXCL13 activates CXCR5, which drives ERK (MAPK signalling) and astrocyte activation in the spinal cord after nerve ligation (Jiang 2016). No paper shows CXCL13 acting on microglial CXCR5, so that arc was removed.

refs.cite: Shen Y et al. 2021, J Neuroinflammation.
Wang J et al. 2023, J Neuroinflammation.
Jiang BC et al. 2016, J Clin Invest.
Shen Y et al. 2020, J Neuroinflammation.

diseases.model: Th17-transfer EAE; CXCR5+PD-1+ T follicular helper cells, CXCL13 antagonism
diseases.shows: CXCR5+ cells infiltrate the CNS in proportion to disease severity and blocking the CXCR5 ligand CXCL13 reduces EAE; CXCR5 here sits on infiltrating lymphocytes, not on the microglia or neurons the map draws.
diseases.cite: Quinn JL et al. 2018, Front Immunol.

proteins.name: VTN
proteins.summary: Vitronectin, a blood and matrix protein, leaks into the brain after cerebral ischaemia. In female mice its knockout reduces microglia and macrophage activation, leukocyte infiltration and striatal IL-6, and IL-6 reverses the protection. In females astrocyte-specific FAK deletion lowers stroke-induced striatal IL-6 by 72%, and a FAK inhibitor gives no extra protection in vitronectin knockouts (Jia 2022); in the subventricular zone the same group found astrocytic FAK lowering IL-6 (Jia 2019), so the sign may depend on the region. The integrin step rests on C6 glioma cells (Keasey 2018). Primary mouse microglia adhere to vitronectin through alphaV integrins and respond with activation markers, MMP-9 and phagocytosis; alphaVbeta3 and alphaVbeta5 are redundant with alphaVbeta1 and alphaVbeta8 (Welser-Alves 2011).
links: Binds alphaV integrins (drawn as ITGAV, the shared alpha chain) on astrocytes, raising IL6 in female mice, and on microglia, promoting phagocytosis (top-level map).
In astrocytes vitronectin binds ITGAV; the complex activates FAK (PTK2, phosphorylated at Y397), and active FAK leads to IL6 transcription by steps not shown (//) (Astrocyte signaling).

refs.cite: Jia C et al. 2020, Stroke.
Jia C et al. 2022, J Cereb Blood Flow Metab.
Jia C et al. 2019, Exp Neurol.
Keasey MP et al. 2018, J Cell Sci.
Welser-Alves JV et al. 2011, J Neuroinflammation.
Milner R et al. 2007, J Immunol.

proteins.name: ACKR3
proteins.summary: CXCR7 (ACKR3) is an atypical chemokine receptor on CNS endothelium that binds CXCL12 and internalises it. In mouse EAE it is raised on the spinal cord endothelium; IL-1beta and IL-17 raise CXCR7-dependent CXCL12 uptake into lysosomes of primary brain endothelial cells, and the CXCR7 antagonist CCX771 keeps abluminal CXCL12, lowers leukocyte entry into the parenchyma and lessens disease. Added (not on the list) as the step that explains how IL-1beta lowers abluminal CXCL12.
links: Driven by IL-1 and IL-17 receptor signalling and lowers CXCL12 on the abluminal side in endothelial cells (top-level map); IL-17A and its receptor IL17RA:IL17RC are drawn again on the endothelium for this.

refs.cite: Cruz-Orengo L et al. 2011, J Exp Med.

proteins.name: ITGAV
proteins.summary: The alphaV integrin chain pairs with beta1, beta3, beta5 and beta8; on primary mouse microglia these alphaV integrins are the main vitronectin receptors and act redundantly (Welser-Alves 2011). Added as the missing partner of vitronectin.
links: Binds vitronectin on astrocytes and microglia (top-level map, Astrocyte signaling).

refs.cite: Welser-Alves JV et al. 2011, J Neuroinflammation.
Milner R et al. 2007, J Immunol.
Jia C et al. 2022, J Cereb Blood Flow Metab.
Keasey MP et al. 2018, J Cell Sci.

proteins.name: HMOX1
proteins.summary: Heme oxygenase-1 in blood-brain barrier endothelium restrains the IL-1 response: IL-1 receptor signalling lowers it, and endothelial Hmox1 deletion raises ACKR1 (DARC), ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 while HO-1 overexpression lowers them, with milder EAE (mouse, Hauptmann 2020). Added (not on the list) as the step between the IL-1 receptor and ACKR1.
links: Lowered by IL-1 receptor signalling and lowers ACKR1 in endothelial cells (top-level map).

refs.cite: Hauptmann J et al. 2020, Acta Neuropathol.

proteins.name: CCL20
proteins.summary: The chemokine CCL20 attracts CCR6-positive Th17 cells. Oncostatin M raises it in inflamed brain endothelial cells and in reactive astrocytes (primary human and mouse cells), and CCL20 activates LFA-1 on Th17 cells and raises their adhesion to the brain endothelium; OSMR-beta-deficient mice have less Th17 infiltration in EAE (Hermans 2022). Added (not on the list) as the step through which OSM recruits Th17 cells.
links: Raised by OSM receptor signalling in endothelial cells and astrocytes and promotes Th17 cell adhesion and recruitment; drawn on the blood side, where it acts on Th17 cells (top-level map).

refs.cite: Hermans D et al. 2022, Acta Neuropathol.

proteins.name: GPNMB
proteins.summary: Glycoprotein NMB is raised in disease-associated microglia. In human iPSC-derived microglia GPNMB sits next to Ser129-phosphorylated alpha-synuclein, and knocking it down in microglia blocks clearance of the aggregates from neurons.
links: Promotes clearance of alpha-synuclein and supports phagocytosis in microglia (top-level map).

refs.cite: Chueh HJ et al. 2026, Sci Transl Med.
Diaz-Ortiz ME et al. 2022, Science.

diseases.model: PS19 tauopathy mice; microglia-specific Gpnmb knockout (CX3CR1-Cre Gpnmb-flox)
diseases.shows: Microglial GPNMB is needed for mitochondria-carrying extracellular vesicle transfer to astrocytes; its deletion impairs astrocyte function and worsens cognition in PS19 mice.
diseases.cite: Liang C et al. 2026, Nat Neurosci.

diseases.model: Human iPSC-derived microglia with Ser129-phosphorylated alpha-synuclein aggregates; GPNMB knockdown
diseases.shows: GPNMB sits next to alpha-synuclein aggregates and its knockdown blocks microglial trogocytosis-mediated clearance of intraneuronal alpha-synuclein.
diseases.cite: Chueh HJ et al. 2026, Sci Transl Med.

proteins.name: TYROBP
proteins.summary: TYROBP (DAP12) is the signalling adaptor of TREM2 and other microglial receptors. In primary mouse microglia a dominant-negative DAP12 abolishes TREM2-driven phagocytosis of apoptotic neurons, and its loss changes disease in amyloid and tau mice.
links: Binds TREM2 and supports phagocytosis in microglia (top-level map).
Needed for the rise of APOE RNA in microglia, also without TREM2; the steps between are not shown, so the step is an unknown process (Microglial phagocytosis).

refs.cite: Takahashi K et al. 2005, J Exp Med.
Cui X et al. 2021, Brain Res Bull.
Audrain M et al. 2021, Alzheimers Dement.

diseases.model: Microglial TREM2 and DAP12 knockout AD model mice; primary microglia with Abeta1-42
diseases.shows: Microglial DAP12 (TYROBP) knockout changes inflammatory cytokine output and Abeta plaque deposition in AD model mice, the TREM2-TYROBP signalling step the map draws.
diseases.cite: Cui X et al. 2020, Brain Res Bull.

proteins.name: CD9
proteins.summary: Tetraspanin CD9 marks synapse-engulfing microglia. After cortical injury in mice, deleting CD9 in microglia or blocking it reduces synapse engulfment, synapse loss and Syk phosphorylation and improves memory.
links: Promotes synapse loss in microglia (top-level map).

refs.cite: Matoba K et al. 2026, Nat Commun.

diseases.model: Humanized APP knock-in AD mice; CD9+ plaque-associated (MGnD) microglia and extracellular vesicles
diseases.shows: CD9 marks the plaque-associated microglia that engulf dystrophic neurites and hyper-secrete CD9+ vesicles carrying phospho-tau; functional CD9 blockade data exist only in the cortical-injury model.
diseases.cite: Clayton K et al. 2021, Mol Neurodegener.

proteins.name: GBA1
proteins.summary: Glucocerebrosidase breaks down glucosylceramide in lysosomes. In microglia, its inhibition makes glucosylceramide accumulate, which lets mitochondrial DNA leak into the cytosol and triggers STING-dependent inflammation and neuron loss, in culture and in mice (Wang 2024). In neurons, GCase loss slows the lysosomal degradation of alpha-synuclein, and alpha-synuclein in turn blocks GCase trafficking to the lysosome (Mazzulli 2011).
links: Breaks down glucosylceramide in the phagolysosome; glucosylceramide activates STING by steps not shown (//, mitochondrial DNA release), and active STING drives microglial activation (NLRP3 inflammasome).
Needed for the lysosomal degradation of alpha-synuclein by cathepsin D in neurons, by a mechanism not shown (dashed catalysis) (Neuron signaling).

refs.cite: Mazzulli JR et al. 2011, Cell.
Wang R et al. 2024, Sci Signal.

diseases.model: Patient-derived and GBA1-mutant neurons, GCase knockdown and alpha-synuclein manipulation (synucleinopathy models)
diseases.shows: Low GCase raises alpha-synuclein and alpha-synuclein in turn inhibits GCase, the bidirectional GBA1-alpha-synuclein loop the map draws.
diseases.cite: Mazzulli JR et al. 2011, Cell.

proteins.name: GALC
proteins.summary: Galactosylceramidase is the enzyme lost in Krabbe disease. GALC-deficient microglia fail to raise TREM2 and clear myelin debris after demyelination, and GALC-null astrocytes overexpress lipocalin-2.
links: Supports TREM2 induction in microglia (top-level map).
Its loss raises LCN2 transcription in astrocytes by a mechanism not shown: unknown process (?) (Astrocyte signaling).

Breaks down psychosine (galactosylsphingosine), drawn as psychosine to sphingosine catalysed by GALC; astrocytes made from Krabbe patients' stem cells accumulate psychosine (Lieberman 2022). Psychosine raises iNOS in primary astrocytes by a mechanism not shown: unknown process (?) on NOS2 transcription (Giri 2008) (Astrocyte signaling).

refs.cite: Scott-Hewitt NJ et al. 2017, Hum Mol Genet.
Favret J et al. 2024, Sci Rep.
Lieberman R et al. 2022, PLoS One.
Giri S et al. 2008, J Neurochem.

diseases.model: GALC +/- mice (MS risk variant model), cuprizone demyelination and remyelination
diseases.shows: Heterozygous GALC mice clear myelin debris poorly and remyelinate less after cuprizone, with a blunted microglial phagocytic response and reduced Trem2, linking the MS risk gene GALC to microglial myelin clearance.
diseases.cite: Scott-Hewitt NJ et al. 2017, Hum Mol Genet.

proteins.name: PLIN2
proteins.summary: Perilipin 2 coats lipid droplets in microglia. Its knockdown blocks NLRP3 inflammasome activation after ischaemia and in microglia after oxygen-glucose deprivation, and its loss in myelin-laden phagocytes lowers inflammation and improves remyelination.
links: Promotes NLRP3 inflammasome activation in microglia (NLRP3 inflammasome); knockdown blocks it, the mechanism is not shown, so a parallel unknown process (?) carries it.

refs.cite: Liu XY et al. 2023, In Vitro Cell Dev Biol Anim.
Stephens IO et al. 2025, Cells.
Loix M et al. 2022, Cell Mol Life Sci.

diseases.model: CRISPR Plin2-knockout BV2 microglia challenged with AD-related stimuli
diseases.shows: Plin2 loss reduces microglial lipid droplet burden and changes phagocytosis and bioenergetics under AD stimuli; weak (microglial cell line, no in vivo AD model).
diseases.cite: Stephens IO et al. 2025, Cells.

diseases.model: Myelin-laden phagocytes and demyelination/remyelination models; Plin2 loss
diseases.shows: Perilipin-2 limits remyelination by preventing lipid droplet degradation in myelin-laden phagocytes.
diseases.cite: Loix M et al. 2022, Cell Mol Life Sci.

proteins.name: CH25H
proteins.summary: Cholesterol 25-hydroxylase makes 25-hydroxycholesterol. In primary mouse microglia TLR4 signalling induces it strongly; 25-HC raises mature IL-1beta and IL-1alpha after priming, without changing pro-IL-1beta, NLRP3 or ASC, acting upstream of K+ efflux and caspase-1 (ASC specks; the inflammasome is not shown to be NLRP3), more strongly with apoE4 (Wong 2020, read in full). Its deletion rescues tau neurodegeneration. 25-HC is anti-inflammatory in peripheral macrophages, so the sign is microglia-specific.
links: Induced by TLR4 signalling and promotes inflammasome activation in microglia (top-level map).

Made under TLR4 signalling (omitted process, //; the adaptor was not tested, so the box is TLR4 signalling, not the MyD88-dependent one); converts cholesterol to 25-hydroxycholesterol, which promotes inflammasome activation by a mechanism not shown (?) upstream of K+ efflux and caspase-1 (NLRP3 inflammasome).

refs.cite: Wong MY et al. 2020, J Neuroinflammation.
Romero J et al. 2024, J Neuroinflammation.
Zhang H et al. 2026, Neurosci Bull.

diseases.model: MPTP and alpha-synuclein preformed fibril mouse models; astrocyte-specific Ch25h conditional knockout and knockdown; PD patient iPSC-derived astrocytes
diseases.shows: Astrocytic CH25H is raised in PD and its conditional knockout or knockdown reduces dopaminergic neuron loss and motor deficits by freeing p62 for autophagic degradation of alpha-synuclein.
diseases.cite: Zhang X et al. 2026, Sci Transl Med.

proteins.name: IRF1
proteins.summary: Interferon regulatory factor 1 is induced by IFN-gamma in astrocytes and binds inflammatory gene promoters. Astrocyte-specific Irf1 deletion limits blood-brain barrier disruption after injury, and Irf1 knockout reduces EAE and infarct size.
links: Induced by IFN-gamma receptor signalling (top-level map). In the astrocyte nucleus it drives CXCL10 transcription (Astrocyte signaling). The outgoing top-level arc to CXCL10 was removed.
In neurons IRF1 is activated downstream of ZBP1:RIPK3 and drives ACOD1 production (Neuron signaling, Daniels 2019).

refs.cite: Cui W et al. 2025, Sci Transl Med.
Jarosinski KW et al. 2002, J Neuroimmunol.
Dell'Albani P et al. 2001, J Neurosci Res.
Daniels BP et al. 2019, Immunity.

diseases.model: EAE and human MS lesions; astrocytic IRF1 and its repressor BATF2
diseases.shows: Astrocytic IRF1 drives interferon-gamma-induced inflammatory programmes (including caspase-1) in EAE and colocalises with astrocytes in MS lesions; loss of the repressor BATF2 amplifies IRF1 and worsens disease.
diseases.cite: Tinkey RA et al. 2025, Cell Rep.

proteins.name: ZBP1
proteins.summary: Z-DNA binding protein 1 is a sensor that engages RIPK3. In mouse neurons it is needed to restrict neuroinvasive Zika and West Nile virus: ZBP1 loss lowers RIPK3 phosphorylation, and RIPK3 drives IRF1-dependent IRG1 (ACOD1) and itaconate without killing the neuron; MLKL and caspase-8 are dispensable (Daniels 2019, read in full).
links: Binds RIPK3 (RHIM interaction) into ZBP1:RIPK3 (Neuron signaling). The MLKL phosphorylation drawn earlier came from a BV2 microglia virus study and was removed: in neurons the complex does not act through MLKL.

In neurons ZBP1:RIPK3 activates IRF1 by a mechanism not shown (?); active IRF1 drives ACOD1 (IRG1) production (//), ACOD1 makes itaconate from cis-aconitate, and itaconate inhibits succinate dehydrogenase, which restricts the virus without killing the neuron (Neuron signaling; Irf1 knockdown abolished Irg1 induction in primary neurons, Daniels 2019).

refs.cite: Daniels BP et al. 2019, Immunity.

diseases.model: PS19 tauopathy mice; Zbp1 haploinsufficiency; human AD excitatory neurons
diseases.shows: Tau aggregates reactivate transposable elements producing Z-RNAs that activate ZBP1 and kill neurons; Zbp1 haploinsufficiency rescues cognition, the ZBP1-RIPK3 necroptosis route the map draws.
diseases.cite: Liu W et al. 2026, Nat Neurosci.

proteins.name: IFITM3
proteins.summary: Interferon-induced transmembrane protein 3 binds the active gamma-secretase complex near its catalytic site and raises amyloid-beta 40 and 42 production; its knockout lowers gamma-secretase activity and plaques in 5xFAD mice. IFN-gamma and IFN-alpha induce it in primary mouse neurons, and IL-6 and IL-1beta in human astrocytes, where it also raises gamma-secretase activity (Hur 2020, read in full). It has the opposite effect on Notch cleavage.
links: Induced by IFN-gamma receptor signalling and raises amyloid processing in neurons (top-level map).
Induced by IL-1 and IL-6 receptor signalling in astrocytes and raises amyloid-beta production there (top-level map).

refs.cite: Hur JY et al. 2020, Nature.

diseases.model: Human AD brain, APP mouse models and cell models; IFITM3 knockout and overexpression
diseases.shows: IFITM3 binds the gamma-secretase complex and raises Abeta production; its deletion lowers amyloid, the IFITM3-gamma-secretase step the map draws.
diseases.cite: Hur JY et al. 2020, Nature.

proteins.name: CYBB
proteins.summary: CYBB (NOX2, gp91phox) is the catalytic subunit of the microglial and neuronal NADPH oxidase that makes superoxide. In IL-10-deficient mouse microglia NOX2-derived ROS drive NLRP3 inflammasome priming and caspase-1 activation, and in an LPS Parkinson model neuronal NOX2 drives dopaminergic neuron loss, which NOX2-deficient neurons escape.
links: Drives oxidative stress in microglia (top-level map).
As part of NADPH oxidase (CYBB, CYBA, NCF1, NCF2, RAC1) reduces oxygen to ROS in microglia, and the ROS drive NLRP3 inflammasome activation by steps not yet known (NLRP3 inflammasome).
As part of the neuronal NADPH oxidase reduces oxygen to ROS in neurons (Neuron signaling).

refs.cite: Gao Y et al. 2020, Int J Mol Sci.
Tu D et al. 2023, Free Radic Biol Med.

diseases.model: Tg2576 APP-overexpressing mice crossed to Nox2 (Cybb)-null mice
diseases.shows: Deleting the NADPH oxidase catalytic subunit Nox2 in APP mice abolishes the cerebrovascular oxidative stress and rescues neurovascular and behavioural dysfunction, showing NOX2-derived superoxide mediates amyloid-driven damage.
diseases.cite: Park L et al. 2008, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A.

diseases.model: Chronic LPS mouse model of PD and midbrain neuron-glia cultures; neuronal and global NOX2 deletion
diseases.shows: NOX2 is persistently upregulated in microglia and neurons in a PD model and neuronal NOX2 deletion is protective, the superoxide-producing role the map draws.
diseases.cite: Tu D et al. 2023, Free Radic Biol Med.

diseases.model: MOG-induced EAE in Nox2 (Cybb) gene-ablated mice; CNS myeloid cells and microglia
diseases.shows: Nox2 deficiency reduces EAE severity, immune cell infiltration, demyelination and CNS oxidative stress, showing microglial NOX2 drives MS-model pathology.
diseases.cite: Hu CF et al. 2021, Front Immunol.

proteins.name: PECAM1
proteins.full_name: platelet and endothelial cell adhesion molecule 1
proteins.summary: PECAM1 (CD31) is on brain endothelium and leukocytes. After stroke it promotes neutrophil infiltration, and on brain endothelium it stabilises the blood-brain barrier, so its two roles have opposite signs.
links: Promotes infiltration at the blood vessel and stabilises the barrier in endothelial cells (top-level map).

refs.cite: Winneberger J et al. 2021, Brain Behav Immun.
Wimmer I et al. 2019, Front Immunol.

diseases.model: Human MS white and grey matter lesions; human blood-brain barrier endothelial model with PECAM-1 loss; neuroinflammation
diseases.shows: PECAM-1 is strongly upregulated in early MS lesions and stabilises barrier integrity while favouring paracellular T-cell diapedesis, the two opposite-sign roles the map draws.
diseases.cite: Wimmer I et al. 2019, Front Immunol.

proteins.name: MIF
proteins.summary: Macrophage migration inhibitory factor is needed for NLRP3 inflammasome activation and drives TLR4/MyD88/NF-kB signalling in microglia, shown by knockdown in microglia and in an MPTP Parkinson model.
links: Promotes TLR4 signalling in microglia (top-level map). Its direct NLRP3 binding needs an intracellular MIF pool and is drawn as a pending micro-map.

refs.cite: Huang Y et al. 2025, Commun Biol.
Huang H et al. 2021, Nan Fang Yi Ke Da Xue Xue Bao.
Zhou F et al. 2025, Anesthesiol Res Pract.

diseases.model: MPTP/MPP+ PD models and microglia; MIF knockdown
diseases.shows: MIF downregulation attenuates microglial neuroinflammation through TLR4/MyD88/TRAF6/NF-kB and protects dopaminergic neurons, matching the drawn MIF-NLRP3/NF-kB role.
diseases.cite: Huang Y et al. 2025, Commun Biol.

diseases.model: MOG-induced EAE in MIF-deficient mice; CNS effector mechanisms
diseases.shows: MIF-deficient mice mount normal peripheral myelin-specific responses but develop much milder EAE with less CNS inflammation, showing MIF potentiates autoimmune neuroinflammation in the CNS.
diseases.cite: Cox GM et al. 2013, J Immunol.

proteins.name: POMC
proteins.summary: The POMC peptide alpha-MSH, through the melanocortin-4 receptor, dampens astrocyte inflammation. It lowers iNOS and NO in primary astrocytes, and astrocyte-specific MC4R knockdown in EAE removes its suppression of NF-kB signalling. The active peptide is alpha-MSH, cleaved from POMC.
links: Acts through MC4R to lower NF-kB signalling in astrocytes (top-level map).
Cleaved to alpha-MSH, which binds MC4R on astrocytes; the complex lowers NOS2 transcription through cAMP signalling, steps not shown (//) (Astrocyte signaling).

refs.cite: Caruso C et al. 2007, Endocrinology.
Wang Y et al. 2025, J Neuroinflammation.
Khalife MR et al. 2025, eNeuro.

diseases.model: 5XFAD and 3xTg AD mice, chronic NDP-alpha-MSH (POMC-derived melanocortin analogue)
diseases.shows: The alpha-MSH analogue improves cognition and lowers microgliosis and phospho-tau in advanced AD mice, the anti-inflammatory melanocortin action the map draws; the analogue is not MC4R-selective.
diseases.cite: Daini E et al. 2023, Front Immunol.

diseases.model: MPTP+LPS mouse PD model, systemic NDP-MSH (non-brain-penetrant melanocortin agonist), Treg depletion
diseases.shows: Melanocortin receptor activation with an alpha-MSH analogue attenuates striatal dopamine depletion and modulates immune responses in a PD model; acts through MC1R rather than the MC4R drawn.
diseases.cite: Srivastava P et al. 2023, J Neuroimmune Pharmacol.

diseases.model: EAE mouse model of MS; astrocyte-specific MC4R knockdown
diseases.shows: The melanocortin (alpha-MSH)-MC4R axis on astrocytes limits blood-brain barrier disruption and neuroinflammation in EAE; astrocytic MC4R knockdown removes the protection.
diseases.cite: Wang Y et al. 2025, J Neuroinflammation.

proteins.name: CXCL16
proteins.summary: CXCL16 is made by microglia and macrophages and recruits CXCR6-positive CD8 T cells into the injured and amyloid-laden brain. It also makes astrocytes release CCL2.
links: Recruits CD8 T cells through CXCR6 (top-level map).
Binds CXCR6 on astrocytes; the complex raises CCL2 transcription by a mechanism not shown (?) (Astrocyte signaling).

refs.cite: Ge X et al. 2025, Neuron.
Zattoni M et al. 2025, Sci Rep.
Rosito M et al. 2012, J Neurosci.

proteins.name: CSF1
proteins.summary: Colony-stimulating factor 1, made by injured neurons, drives microglial proliferation and activation through CSF1R. Its receptor sits only on microglia in the CNS, and TYROBP lies downstream.
links: Binds CSF1R on microglia (top-level map).

refs.cite: Guan Z et al. 2016, Nat Neurosci.
Chu CH et al. 2016, Brain Behav Immun.

diseases.model: Mouse EAE spinal cord; viral overexpression of CSF1 in spinal neurons
diseases.shows: Neuron-derived CSF1 is raised in EAE and its overexpression drives microglial proliferation and activation with microglia enwrapping CSF1-expressing neurons, followed by neuronal loss and demyelination.
diseases.cite: Gushchina S et al. 2018, Glia.

proteins.name: CCL4
proteins.summary: CCL4 (MIP-1beta) is a microglial chemokine. Through CCR5 it drives microglial engulfment of synapses and, on neurons, blocks autophagy, shown with knockdown, overexpression and the CCR5 blocker maraviroc.
links: Acts through CCR5 to drive synapse loss (top-level map).
Binds CCR5 on neurons, leading to mTOR activation and a block of autophagy (Neuron signaling).

refs.cite: Cao Y et al. 2026, J Neuroinflammation.
Jo M et al. 2017, J Neurosci.

proteins.name: MC4R
proteins.summary: The melanocortin-4 receptor is the alpha-MSH receptor on astrocytes and neurons. Astrocyte-specific MC4R knockdown in EAE and MC4R knockout with cell-specific rescue show that it lowers NF-kB signalling and iNOS. Added as the missing partner of POMC, after it passed the bar by itself.
links: Binds alpha-MSH and lowers NF-kB signalling in astrocytes (top-level map).
Binds alpha-MSH on astrocytes (MC4R-overexpressing primary astrocytes, astrocyte-specific knockdown, Wang 2025); the complex lowers NOS2 transcription by steps not shown (//) (Astrocyte signaling).

refs.cite: Caruso C et al. 2007, Endocrinology.
Khalife MR et al. 2025, eNeuro.
Wang Y et al. 2025, J Neuroinflammation.
Chen S et al. 2018, J Neuroinflammation.

diseases.model: EAE mouse model of MS; astrocyte-specific MC4R knockdown
diseases.shows: Astrocytic MC4R knockdown in EAE removes the protection against blood-brain barrier disruption and neuroinflammation, showing MC4R lowers NF-kB-driven astrocyte inflammation in an MS model.
diseases.cite: Wang Y et al. 2025, J Neuroinflammation.

proteins.name: CXCR6
proteins.summary: CXCR6 is the CXCL16 receptor on CD8 T cells. In 5xFAD mice its loss removes brain CD8 T cells, raises amyloid and worsens memory, with more microglial TNF. Added as the missing partner of CXCL16, after it passed the bar by itself.
links: Binds CXCL16 and drives CD8 T cell accumulation (top-level map).
On astrocytes binds CXCL16 (shown with cxcr6 gfp/gfp astrocyte cocultures, Rosito 2012); the complex raises CCL2 release by a mechanism not shown (?) (Astrocyte signaling).

refs.cite: Su W et al. 2023, Nat Immunol.
Ge X et al. 2025, Neuron.
Rosito M et al. 2012, J Neurosci.

diseases.model: 5xFAD mice; Cxcr6 knockout and bone-marrow chimeras; brain CD8 T cells
diseases.shows: CXCR6 is needed for CD8 T cell residency in the AD brain; its loss removes brain CD8 T cells, raises amyloid and worsens memory with more microglial TNF, the CXCL16-CXCR6 edge the map draws.
diseases.cite: Su W et al. 2023, Nat Immunol.

proteins.name: CSF1R
proteins.summary: CSF1R is the microglial receptor for CSF1 (and IL34). Its inhibition and microglia-restricted knockout change microglial number and state, and CSF1 acting on it raises ERK and changes microglial TNF, NO and IL-1beta output. Added as the missing partner of CSF1, after it passed the bar by itself.
links: Binds CSF1 and drives MAPK signalling and phagocytosis in microglia (top-level map).

refs.cite: Guan Z et al. 2016, Nat Neurosci.

proteins.name: CCR5
proteins.summary: CCR5 is a receptor for CCL3, CCL4 and CCL5. On neurons, microglial chemokines bind it and block autophagy through mTORC1 in Huntington and tau models, rescued by maraviroc (Festa 2023). On microglia CCL4 binding CCR5 drives engulfment of excitatory synapses in rats with chronic kidney disease (Cao 2026, male rats). It is protective in some other CNS models, so the sign depends on the setting. Added as the missing partner of CCL4, after it passed the bar by itself.
links: Binds CCL4 and drives synapse loss in microglia (top-level map).
In neurons CCL4 binds CCR5; the complex activates mTOR by steps not shown (//), and active mTOR blocks autophagy (Neuron signaling).

refs.cite: Cao Y et al. 2026, J Neuroinflammation.
Festa BP et al. 2023, Neuron.
Jo M et al. 2017, J Neurosci.

proteins.disease_note: The direction differs by disease and mechanism: neuronal CCR5 blocks autophagy in the tau model (drawn), while CCR5-deficient mice fare worse after MPTP through a different route (more astrocytic MAO-B, so more toxin activated), which the map does not draw.

diseases.model: Tauopathy (and Huntington) mouse models and neurons; CCR5 knockout and the CCR5 blocker maraviroc
diseases.shows: Microglia-derived CCL3/4/5 activate neuronal CCR5, raising mTORC1 and blocking autophagy and clearance of aggregate-prone proteins; CCR5 loss or maraviroc restores autophagy in the tau model.

diseases.shows: CCR5-deficient mice have fewer nigral dopaminergic neurons, more microglial activation, greater dopamine depletion and worse behaviour after MPTP, so here CCR5 is protective - the opposite sign to the pro-inflammatory CCR5 role the map draws, and MPTP-induced TH cell loss itself was barely changed.

proteins.name: AXL
proteins.summary: The TAM receptor AXL, which recognises phosphatidylserine, is on more than 90% of the CD9-high synapse-engulfing microglia in the mouse thalamus after cortical injury. The AXL inhibitor bemcentinib (R428) lowered synapse engulfment and raised glutamatergic synapse numbers without changing the number of these microglia (in vivo, mostly female mice).
links: Drives synapse loss from microglia (top-level map).

refs.cite: Matoba K et al. 2026, Nat Commun.

proteins.name: FCGR3A
proteins.summary: After cortical injury, blood-brain barrier leakage lets IgG into the thalamus, and Fc-gamma receptor III on microglia drives the CD9-high synapse-engulfing state: an intra-thalamic FcgammaRIII-blocking antibody lowered CD9-high microglia and PSD95 engulfment, raised glutamatergic synapses and improved memory (mouse, in vivo). Drawn as FCGR3A, the human gene for mouse Fcgr3.
links: Raises CD9 on microglia, which drives synapse loss (top-level map).

refs.cite: Matoba K et al. 2026, Nat Commun.

proteins.name: IL34
proteins.summary: Interleukin-34 is the second CSF1R ligand, made by neurons. In primary mouse neuron-glia cultures IL-34, like CSF1 from neurons and astrocytes, makes microglia tolerant to repeated endotoxin through CSF1R and ERK (Chu 2016, read in full). Added (not on the list) beside CSF1.
links: Binds CSF1R on microglia (top-level map).
